questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Recurrence Relation For a Second-Order Differential Equation
questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation ${y}^{″}-y=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for ${a}_{n}$ can be written as

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{f(n)},\,n=0,1,2…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find ${y}^{″}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-2.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+2)(m+1){a}_{m+2}{x}^{m}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}-{a}_{n}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}-{a}_{n}=0.
$$

Finally then, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{(n+1)(n+2)},\,n=0,1,2…
$$

Therefore, $f(n)=(n+1)(n+2).$

questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $18{y}^{″}-9y=0.$  Find $f(n),$ given that the recurrence relation for ${a}_{n}$ can be written as

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{f(n)},\,n=0,1,2…
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we find ${y}^{″}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
18{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }n(n-1){a}_{n}{x}^{n-2}-9{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-2.$ This gives

$$
18{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+2)(m+1){a}_{m+2}{x}^{m}-9{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
18{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}{x}^{n}-9{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[18(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}-9{a}_{n}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
18(n+2)(n+1){a}_{n+2}-9{a}_{n}=0.
$$

Finally then, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+2}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{2(n+1)(n+2)},\,n=0,1,2…
$$

Therefore, $f(n)=2(n+1)(n+2).$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Recurrence Relation For a First-Order Differential Equation
questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $5{y}^{′}-2xy=0.$

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=1,2,3,…$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{′}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}-2x{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }5n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }2{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }5(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }2{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}=0.
$$

Now, in the second series, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n+1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }5(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}-{\sum }_{m=1}^{\infty }2{a}_{m-1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in both summations (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }5(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Next, we need to get two series starting with the same value of $n.$ So, we take out the term $n=0$ from the left-hand side:

$$
5{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }5(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We now combine the series, as follows:

$$
5{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[5(n+1){a}_{n+1}-2{a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Finally, by equating coefficients of ${x}^{n},$ we obtain

$$
{a}_{1}=0,\,5(n+1){a}_{n+1}=2{a}_{n-1}.
$$

Solving for ${a}_{n+1}$ gives

$$
{a}_{n+1}=\frac{2{a}_{n-1}}{5(n+1)},\,n=1,2,3,….
$$

Note that every coefficient with an odd index is equal to $0,$ since ${a}_{1}=0.$

questions.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $xy+9{y}^{′}=0.$

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=1,2,3,…$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{′}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}+9{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }9n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the second sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}+{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }9(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Now, in the first series, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n+1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=1}^{\infty }{a}_{m-1}{x}^{m}+{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }9(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in both summations (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }9(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Next, we need to get two series starting with the same value of $n.$ So, we take out the term $n=0$ from the right-hand side:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}+9{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }9(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We now combine the series, as follows:

$$
9{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[{a}_{n-1}+9(n+1){a}_{n+1}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Finally, by equating coefficients of ${x}^{n},$ we obtain

$$
{a}_{1}=0,\,9(n+1){a}_{n+1}=-{a}_{n-1}.
$$

Solving for ${a}_{n+1}$ gives

$$
{a}_{n+1}=-\frac{{a}_{n-1}}{9(n+1)},\,n=1,2,3,….
$$

Note that every coefficient with an odd index is equal to $0,$ since ${a}_{1}=0.$

Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation ${y}^{′}+2xy=0.$

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=1,2,3…$

First, we find ${y}^{′}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}+2x{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0 \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }2{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}+{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }2{a}_{n}{x}^{n+1}=0.
$$

Now, in the second series, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n+1.$ This gives

$$
{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}+{\sum }_{m=1}^{\infty }2{a}_{m-1}{x}^{m}=0.
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in both summations (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}=0.
$$

Next, we need to get two series starting with the same value of $n.$ So, we take out the term $n=0$ from the left-hand side:

$$
{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2{a}_{n-1}{x}^{n}=0
$$

We now combine the series, as follows:

$$
{a}_{1}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[(n+1){a}_{n+1}+2{a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n}=0
$$

Finally, by equating coefficients of ${x}^{n},$ we obtain

$$
{a}_{1}=0,\,(n+1){a}_{n+1}=-2{a}_{n-1}.
$$

Solving for ${a}_{n+1}$ gives

$$
{a}_{n+1}=\frac{-2{a}_{n-1}}{n+1},\,n=1,2,3….
$$

Note that every coefficient with an odd index is equal to $0,$ since ${a}_{1}=0.$
